title: Pull a string tighter
hook: Change string tension and predict wave speed.
misconception: wave speed doubles when string tension doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply v = √(T/μ) to compare wave speed when string tension changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a taut flexible string with fixed linear mass density, v = √(T/μ). When string tension doubles, wave speed becomes √2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model v = √(T/μ); scaling exponent 0.5. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a taut flexible string with fixed linear mass density, with a nonzero initial result. If string tension triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on wave speed?
recall.why: Apply v = √(T/μ) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is √3.
